title: Arrow function this behaviour
learningObjectives: Explain arrow function this behaviour and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: Arrow functions do not create their own this, arguments, super, or new.target bindings. They capture this lexically from the surrounding scope. This is useful for callbacks but means arrow functions are usually not suitable as object methods that need a dynamic receiver.
understand.whyItMatters: Lexical this avoids common callback binding problems, but using an arrow function as a method can produce unexpected results when the method expects this to refer to the object.
understand.analogy: An arrow function borrows the surrounding function's this rather than receiving a new one when called.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.
